next_step: Final post-mortem and archive - customer decided vendor; follow-up for future SLA discussion Q3
notes:
Deal status: stalled -> closed-lost to competitor (OpenAI Realtime); technical fit primary reason.

Background:
- Large enterprise contact center platform; goal: migrate high-volume chat assistants to Redwood for cost predictability + multi-region routing.
- Requirements: p95 end-to-end response latency <= 200ms for streaming user-facing tokens at production QPS (avg 350 RPS burst to 1k), region failover, and audit logs.

Timeline / recent activity (CRM-style):
- 2024-09-12: Intro call (AE Maya + SE Liam). Discussed architecture, dataset sizes. Customer emphasized strict p95 for interactive UX.
- 2024-10-03: Technical deep-dive with infra team. Shared perf targets and sample traces. Action: sandbox access + dataset for perf run. (Drive deck link above).
- 2024-10-12: POC kickoff call (Fireflies ff_2024-10-12_8432). Agreed scope: 2-week perf POC against 3 hottest flows.
- 2024-10-20: POC deploy (dedicated trial hardware). Initial results: cold-starts ok, but streaming p95 spiked. Logged INF-2134.
- 2024-11-01: Perf run #1: observed p95 ~480-620ms for user-facing streaming events at realistic QPS; customer target 200ms. Detailed traces show chunking overhead and delayed first-byte in some shards.
- 2024-11-08: SE optimizations attempted: kernel selection tweaks, smaller decode chunk sizes, reduced batching, turned on prefix KV caching. Marginal improvements: p95 down to ~360-420ms; still > target. INF-2248 opened for investigation.
- 2024-11-20: Customer performed side-by-side against OpenAI Realtime and internal optimized endpoint. OpenAI Realtime met interactive SLO in their test; internal infra also had lower p95 in same environment. Customer started leaning to competitor.
- 2024-12-10: Exec check-in. Customer cites lack of clear roadmap commitment that would close the p95 gap within their procurement timeline. No internal champion to hold procurement open.
- 2025-01-14: Final meeting. Stratos signals procurement freeze and decision to go with OpenAI Realtime for immediate needs.

Technical notes / root causes observed:
- Main failure mode: streaming latency spikes from "first byte" and intermittent shard-level backpressure when continuous batching kicked in under burst.
- Batching vs latency tradeoff: when trying to reduce p95 we disabled batching aggressively which increased cost; customer unwilling to accept higher unit cost.
- KV/prefix caching not effective: prompt variability dominated so cache hit rate low.
- Kernel path differences: their workload had many short responses; our optimized kernels favored longer token sequences leading to inefficiencies at low per-request token counts.
- Region routing added 10-30ms in some flows due to cross-region fallback; footprint mismatch between their region expectations and Redwood's available capacity during the POC.

Sales/Commercial notes:
- Price was secondary; primary blocker was inability to show demonstrable p95 improvement within procurement window. Customer repeatedly: "UX is non-negotiable — 200ms is table stakes."
- No security blockers: SOC2/KMS/SAML acceptable. Audit logs ok. Team said Redwood's compliance posture was fine.
- There was no active executive sponsor after the CTO changed org priorities; internal champion drifted to support ops instead of procurement.

Next steps (internal):
- Post-mortem captured; attach perf artifacts to drive doc.
- Re-engage Q3 2025 to present new kernel/batching improvements once shipped.
- Keep on lost-won list; request reference permission declined.

Last quoted objection from customer: "If we can't get consistent p95 under load without doubling cost, we can't justify migration. We'll stay with the product that preserves our UX."

Short CRM fragments (preferred):
- "POC failed to hit p95 200ms SLO; lost to OpenAI Realtime."
- "SE actions: kernel tuning, batching config, cache attempts — partial gains, not enough."
- "Blockers: latency, streaming, no champion, procurement freeze."
